About Dōgen

Dōgen (1200–1253) was the Japanese founder of the Sōtō school of Zen after studying in Song China under Rujing. Returning to Japan, he established monastic communities culminating at Eiheiji.

How to read this passage

Across 4 recurring voices here (notably Epictetus and Augustine of Hippo), awakening is framed through Vedanta and Stoicism. Some passages define awakening; others warn how it fails; still others relocate it inside habit, community, or language. This passage enters that discussion through awakening, self.
